finding.claim: Authorization result is discarded in dropTable, so any caller reaches the DROP TABLE; the table name is also concatenated into SQL (injection).
finding.source: HTTP request to /admin/drop with form value t, from any user, including one without the dba role

trace.note: route /admin/drop registered to dropTable, no middleware
Authorize(u, "dba") return value ignored, so there is no deny or return
unvalidated t parameter concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its error is not checked. Compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which checks the error and returns 403. There is no allowlist or identifier validation on t. There is no route-level auth middleware. userFrom (api.go:22) does an unchecked type assertion, which panics if no user is in the context, so unauthenticated requests would only cause a panic and not a bypass. No authentication code is present in this file.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement. There is no identifier allowlist, no parameterization, and no middleware. userFrom at api.go:22 has an unchecked type assertion.
verdict.reason: api.go:26 calls Authorize as a bare statement, so a non-dba user passes straight to the unvalidated concatenation at api.go:27, unlike the checked vacuum at api.go:33-36. Caveat: nothing in this single file ever sets the "user" context value (main at api.go:43-46 has no wrapper), so as written every request panics at api.go:22 and the real exposure depends on external auth middleware that puts a user in the context.
